answer: Agents can anchor admission to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when an identity is caught double-signing or fabricating work. Each agent commits stake before receiving tasks; peers cross-check signed outputs, and a fraud proof triggers a deterministic penalty. A whisper about suspicious behavior can start a ripple of independent audits across the garden, but the attacker must lock real capital for every identity and risks losing it, making a large Sybil swarm expensive rather than merely easy to mint.
